statement: Verification is evidence, not a support guarantee.
rule: A tuple (React adapter, exact React, Pixi adapter, exact pixi.js) is verified on a render backend when its cell passed on that backend in this record (every command, every conformance scenario and the render check) and every boundary probe and every negative case of this record behaved as expected. A backend run that applied an environment shim (adapterMatrix.environmentShims, a labelled workaround for an upstream pixi.js bug) is judged like any other: a pass verifies the tuple, which carries the shim id, and a failure is a failure. A run a record before 2026-10-11 lists as an expected blank render (the retired expectedBlankRender list) verifies nothing. Each tuple lists every backend it is verified on; backends are never inferred from each other.

rendering.note: Software rendering: no GPU took part. WebGL ran on ANGLE over SwiftShader and WebGPU on Dawn over SwiftShader's Vulkan device, a fallback adapter (isFallbackAdapter true). It counts as verification; a run on a real GPU (run-cells.mjs --gpu hardware) can be added later as extra evidence.

environment.os: Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS (container in a Firecracker microVM)
environment.cpu: 4 vCPU Intel(R) Xeon(R) Processor @ 2.10GHz, 15 GiB RAM
environment.gpu: none: no GPU device in the machine (/dev/dri absent); every backend renders in software

backends.webgl: WebGL 2.0 through ANGLE on SwiftShader: 'ANGLE (Google, Vulkan 1.3.0 (SwiftShader Device (Subzero) (0x0000C0DE)), SwiftShader driver)'; flags --use-gl=angle --use-angle=swiftshader --enable-unsafe-swiftshader
backends.webgpu: Dawn on SwiftShader's Vulkan device: adapter vendor 'google', architecture 'swiftshader', isFallbackAdapter true (a software fallback adapter); flags as WebGL plus --enable-unsafe-webgpu --enable-features=Vulkan --use-vulkan=swiftshader --use-webgpu-adapter=swiftshader. Without those flags headless Chromium exposes navigator.gpu (secure contexts) but requestAdapter() returns null

commands: node design/compatibility/cells/run-cells.mjs run --tier nightly --patches all --cell <a third of the cells> --no-cache --work <work> --tarballs <work>/tarballs   (three shards in parallel)
notes: Tier: nightly with `--patches all` (297 cells: every React adapter, React 18.0 to 19.3, at its minimum and latest audited patch x the newest audited patch of every Pixi 8 minor and pixi.js 7.2.0, 7.2.4, 7.3.0, 7.3.3, 7.4.2 and 7.4.3), a superset of the scheduled nightly tier's 216 cells. Render backends: WebGL and WebGPU; Pixi 7 cells WebGL only.

First record with environment shims (adapterMatrix.environmentShims, owner ruling 2026-10-11): every WebGPU run of the pixi-8 adapter with pixi.js >=8.2.6 <8.10.0 (88 runs: 8.2.6, 8.3.4, 8.4.1, 8.5.2, 8.6.6, 8.7.3, 8.8.1 and 8.9.2 x 11 React versions) applied pixi-webgpu-texture-units, which clamps WebGL MAX_TEXTURE_IMAGE_UNITS to 16 before Pixi initializes; each reported 32 -> 16. No WebGL run and no run on pixi.js 8.10+ applied it.

Same machine and software profile as the 2026-10-10 records, which it supersedes (only the newest record of a machine and GPU profile counts). Those ran without the shim and keep their 64 and 88 WebGPU expected blank renders on 8.2-8.9 as recorded.

Commit 10cd4a4 on claude/webgpu-texture-units-shim, run from a separate worktree of that commit. Fresh: a new work directory, packages rebuilt with `pnpm build --force`, tarballs packed from that build, `--no-cache` (no verdict reused), CI=true. The npm download cache was shared (registry tarballs are integrity-checked).

Three cell shards (every third cell each) ran in parallel on 4 vCPUs with the probes (cells 02:18 to 03:04 UTC, 46 minutes), then the negative cases and the data-only probes. No test timed out and no failure was retried.

Cells with React 18.0.0, 18.1.0 and 18.2.0 ran with harness/test/lend-act.ts; Pixi 7.2 cells compiled the Pixi 7 type consumer without the pixi8-names-rejected assertions (typeAssertions, from 7.3.0), as in 2026-10-10.2.

Commits after this one change documentation, generated tables, the verification tooling and tests only; `node design/compatibility/verification.mjs compare --record 2026-10-11 --tarballs <fresh pack>` shows whether a later commit packs the same code (Markdown and build logs aside).

negatives.message: @pixi-react-provisional/react-19.3 supports React 19.3.x (tested: 19.3.0), but React 19.1.9 is installed. Install and use the adapter package that matches the installed React minor (for example @pixi-react-provisional/react-19.1).

@pixi-react-provisional/react-18.0 supports React 18.0.x (tested: 18.0.0), but React 18.3.1 is installed. Install and use the adapter package that matches the installed React minor (for example @pixi-react-provisional/react-18.3).
The Pixi 8 adapter does not support this installation: pixi.js 8.5.0 is excluded: its ParticleContainer.destroy fails (fixed by 8.5.2).

dataOnly.statement: Data only, not verified: these results are never verification, never enter verifiedRanges and never change a peer range.
dataOnly.description: Data-only probes (issue 17). Each probe installs the packed adapters beside a React or pixi.js the adapter does not declare, ignoring peers, and records what every cell command does. The adapters' environment checks are bypassed in the conformance run only (cell.json dataOnly.bypassEnvironmentCheck), so the suite shows what would happen past them. Results are data, never verification: nothing here enters verifiedRanges or changes a peer range.

groups.description: The Pixi 7 adapter on pixi.js releases outside its peer range: the highest patch of 7.0 and 7.1 (below the 7.2.0 floor), and the excluded 7.4.0 (7.4.1 was never published to npm). Pixi 7.2 and 7.3, and React 18.0 to 18.2, were data-only probes until they became matrix cells (React 18 per-minor packages, the Pixi 7 range widened to 7.2).

findings: pixi.js 7.4.0: the adapter's entry fails to import in plain Node ('Worker is not defined', a pixi.js 7.4.0 module-scope dependency on a browser global); in Chromium, past checkEnvironment(), the whole suite passes with React 18.3.1 and 19.3.0; types pass. It stays excluded from the peer range.

pixi.js 7.1.4 and 7.0.5: the adapter cannot load. pixi.js 7.1 does not export HTMLText, and 7.0 does not export the filters or HTMLText from its root, which the adapter's entry imports by name: Node import and the browser build fail, so no conformance scenario ran. Types also fail.
pixi.js 7.4.1 was never published to npm, so nothing ran for it.
WebGL: all 297 cells passed (every command, every conformance scenario, the render check).

WebGPU: all 231 Pixi 8 cells passed and are verified on WebGPU, every React adapter and patch on every Pixi 8 minor. The 88 runs on pixi.js 8.2.6 to 8.9.2 applied the environment shim pixi-webgpu-texture-units (WebGL MAX_TEXTURE_IMAGE_UNITS 32 clamped to 16) and rendered the red rectangle; in 2026-10-10.2, without the shim, the same 88 runs showed a blank canvas. They carry the footnote: WebGPU on pixi.js <8.10 needs the workaround for pixijs/pixijs#11389 (fixed in 8.10.0); without it, WebGPU renders a blank canvas on devices whose WebGL texture-unit count exceeds their WebGPU per-stage limit. Use pixi.js 8.10+ or WebGL.

The shim changes nothing in the adapters or the checks: every conformance scenario ran as written, and the WebGL runs and the pixi.js 8.10.2 to 8.22.0 WebGPU runs, which apply no shim, passed as in 2026-10-10.2.

Rendering was software throughout (no GPU in the machine): WebGL on ANGLE/SwiftShader, WebGPU on SwiftShader's fallback adapter. Owner ruling: software rendering counts as verification; the Apple M5 Max hardware record adds real-GPU evidence and stays valid without re-running (it rendered pixi.js 8.2–8.9 on WebGPU without the shim, so its WebGL presumably reports at most 16 texture units and the shim would be a no-op; not yet measured).
Boundary probes: 51 of 51 passed (pixi-8.5.0 by failing exactly as the audit recorded). Incompatible pairs: 7 of 7 rejected as expected.
